items.title: Introducing System One Models & Jev
items.claim: TypeSafe positions Jev as a fast structured-decision model for software and reports early-access, price, and latency claims.

items.title: TypeSafe primitives
items.claim: The official primitive contract describes Choice, Score, and Noul typed decisions.

items.title: System One Adapter
items.claim: TypeSafe publishes a drop-in interface backed by other LLM APIs for comparison, not an open Jev model.

items.title: SemIf, formerly OpenJev
items.claim: An independent open-model project reproduces a Jev-like interface pattern and explicitly says it is not Jev or affiliated with TypeSafe.

items.title: mini-Jev
items.claim: A MIT-licensed Qwen3-4B teaching experiment reads option logits and states that its scores are not calibrated probabilities.

items.title: GLiClass
items.claim: GLiClass is an Apache-2.0 local zero-shot sequence classifier, an adjacent alternative rather than a Jev-compatible model.

items.title: Jev Showcase
items.claim: The public repository includes the TypeSafe Jev endpoint, model reference, live-key instructions, and typed examples.

items.title: Jev tool router
items.claim: TypeSafe documents a Jev-backed routing demo and explicitly says the agent and tool execution are mocked.

items.title: Jev use cases
items.claim: The repository documents the public endpoint and implements Choice, Score, and Noul use cases.

items.title: Jev pricing
items.claim: An independent wrapper states its own prepaid pricing and explicitly separates it from direct TypeSafe pricing.

items.title: Jev alternatives
items.claim: An independent guide identifies community Jev-like projects and adjacent classifiers; its list is treated as a lead source requiring direct verification.

items.title: TypeSafe models
items.claim: The current model page names Jev 1.13 / jev-1.13.0, aliases jev-latest and jev-preview, $0.042/M input with free output, 250,000 tokens/second and 1,200 requests/minute, a 64k request context, a 32k state-plus-longest-question limit, and text-only input.

items.title: TypeSafe API reference
items.claim: The API reference documents POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, Bearer API keys, state plus typed questions, model aliases, and 401, 422, 429, and 529 failure conditions.

items.title: TypeSafe console
items.claim: The public console redirects to login and offers Google or email-code sign-in; this establishes a login surface but not a new account's credits or API eligibility.

items.title: TypeSafe homepage
items.claim: On 20 Sep 2026 the homepage repeated the $42 per billion input-token headline and exposed a Join Waitlist path; this historical observation does not establish current signup eligibility.

items.title: TypeSafe legal index
items.claim: The legal index links the Data Processing Addendum, Master Customer Agreement, and Privacy Policy and points to enterprise zero-data-retention information.

items.title: Master Customer Agreement
items.claim: The MCA permits processing of Input to provide services and calculate fees, describes telemetry, fraud/abuse, and legal processing, says Input is not included in training datasets without prior consent, and makes credits and usage limits part of access.

items.title: TypeSafe Privacy Policy
items.claim: The privacy policy says TypeSafe does not train or fine-tune on prompts or Input, may disclose Input to service providers, hosts services in the United States, and retains personal data as reasonably necessary without giving a Jev-specific duration.

items.title: Data Processing Addendum
items.claim: The DPA describes TypeSafe as processor for Customer Personal Data, purpose-based service processing and retention, subprocessors, and international-transfer terms for the relevant customer arrangement.

items.title: OpenRouter Jev 1.13
items.claim: OpenRouter lists typesafe/jev-1.13 at $0.042/M input and $0/M output, with a 32k context and a 2026-09-18 release date; its availability panel is an observation, not a guarantee.

items.title: OpenRouter TypeSafe catalogue
items.claim: The OpenRouter catalogue lists Jev Latest and Jev 1.13 and provides a unified API route; gateway account, routing, logging, and terms remain a separate boundary.

items.title: OpenRouter Jev Lab
items.claim: The Jev Lab documents a two-stage workflow that compiles prompts into typed questions and calls alpha.decisions with typesafe/jev-1.13.

items.title: Cloudflare Jev model page
items.claim: Cloudflare documents the third-party typesafe/jev model with a 32k context, AI.run and REST examples, and example output identifying jev-1.13.0; Jev-specific numeric pricing points to the dashboard.

items.title: Cloudflare AI Gateway
items.claim: Cloudflare says AI Gateway is available on all plans and provides routing, analytics, and logging controls; this does not establish Jev-specific pricing or retention.

items.title: Vercel AI Gateway Jev page
items.claim: The named Vercel Jev page was inaccessible to the direct checker; no current model ID, price, availability, or provider status is accepted from it.

items.title: Independent Jev wrapper pricing
items.claim: On 20 Sep 2026 the report recorded the independent page as not affiliated with TypeSafe, with /api/v1/decide, $0.42/M input, free output, and $5–$100 prepaid packs; it omitted the tier detail recorded on 24 Sep.

items.title: Alternatives verification refresh
items.claim: The 2026-09-21 refresh used supplied local artifacts only; it did not live-check the six retained repositories or documentation sets, so all current project facts remain unknown and no row was upgraded.

items.title: Alternatives verification refresh — negative finding
items.claim: No verified open-weight Jev model was found in this refresh; this is a verification-status negative finding, not evidence that no such model exists.

items.title: System One Adapter
items.claim: The current README describes a drop-in TypeSafeClient replacement backed by OpenAI, Anthropic, or compatible LLM APIs, with Choice, Score, Noul, structured-output modes, retries, and usage/debug fields; this is an adapter rather than Jev weights.

items.title: SemIf (formerly OpenJev)
items.claim: The project describes an independent open-model reproduction of a decision-interface pattern and explicitly says it does not reproduce Jev’s undisclosed model or training; its local/browser paths and full primitive parity remain separate checks.

items.title: SemIf method
items.claim: The method page describes generation-free option readouts and warm RTX 3090 timings with model loading and result writes excluded; these are project measurements, not a Jev benchmark.

items.title: jevlike
items.claim: The repository documents a local trainable option scorer with JSONL context/options/label input, CPU/MPS/CUDA paths, evaluation and calibration commands, and states that its local experiments do not reproduce Jev or TypeSafe’s private training.

items.title: mini-jev
items.claim: The direct repository check was not completed in this refresh; current status, model/weights, contract, licence, runtime, privacy, evaluation, cost, and latency remain unknown.

items.title: GLiClass
items.claim: The current repository documents a generalist text-classification model, label/score/threshold client behavior, downloadable model IDs, Ray Serve deployment, and CPU/GPU-oriented configurations; it does not establish Jev primitives or parity.

items.title: Introducing Structured Outputs in the API
items.claim: OpenAI distinguishes JSON mode from Structured Outputs that conform to a developer-supplied JSON Schema; this establishes a schema boundary, not Jev model parity, calibrated decision correctness, or a current deployment price.

items.title: OpenAI Node Structured Outputs guide
items.claim: The official guide recommends Responses parsing with text.format and documents supported schema constraints; semantic correctness, current price, latency, and provider data terms remain deployment-specific.

items.title: killmyidea Jev client
items.claim: The current source sets the System One endpoint and jev-latest model alias; the application sends state and typed questions through a server-side Jev call.

items.title: killmyidea deployment metadata
items.claim: The checked source documents local, Vercel, and alternate-server paths, a public hostname, production analytics configuration, and SQLite archive design; these are deployment metadata, not proof of a live service or adoption.

items.title: killmyidea public host access check
items.claim: The public host and the attempted robots.txt, favicon.ico, and api/stats paths were not accessible to this checker; no live status was accepted.

items.title: Jev Showcase direct-source audit
items.claim: The repository documents Jev endpoint/model wiring and optional live calls, but its main paths are local or Docker and it identifies itself as an unofficial TypeSafe companion; no public deployment or production trace was found.

items.title: TypeSafe playground tool-router boundary
items.claim: The document describes a Jev-backed routing step but explicitly says agent and tool execution are mocked, with no production credentials or real tools; it is a repository demo.

items.title: jev-usecases reference-harness boundary
items.claim: The MIT repository documents Jev endpoint/model use and live fixture instructions, while its README states that the initial implementation is not a claim that procedures, labels, or thresholds are ready for unattended production.

items.title: Awesome Jev lead index
items.claim: The directory was used only as an index for leads. Its entries, stars, screenshots, and labels were not accepted as direct evidence of Jev use, deployment, or adoption.

items.title: Jev adoption audit negative finding
items.claim: No checked source met the catalogue bar for a verified production product: explicit Jev use plus direct evidence of operation beyond a local, mocked, or reference project and a named product or organisation using it.

items.title: Builder fit and maintenance synthesis
items.claim: Run run:c4d2041e-27de-485b-9190-087eb8bb275a, recorded at runs/2026/09/c4d2041e-27de-485b-9190-087eb8bb275a/report.md, synthesizes the 20 September access record, 22 September alternatives audit, and 23 September product audit into a dated builder decision branch and proposed maintenance rules.

items.title: Builder fit synthesis — measurement boundary
items.claim: The report at runs/2026/09/c4d2041e-27de-485b-9190-087eb8bb275a/report.md records that no independent workload measurement, common comparison, or authenticated Jev call was run.

items.title: TypeSafe MCA, displayed Sep 23 update
items.claim: On 24 Sep the MCA displayed Last updated Sep 23, 2026. Current text permits service/fee processing and telemetry, restricts model-weight training on Customer Data without consent, and includes credit expiry terms. The exact diff from the Sep 19 body is unknown.

items.title: Independent proxy pricing tiers
items.claim: On 24 Sep the independent, non-TypeSafe-affiliated page self-reported $0.42/M input for $5/$10/$20 packs, $0.35/M for $50, and $0.25/M for $100, with free output. Whether tiers existed on 20 Sep and actual purchase/data terms are unknown.

items.title: TypeSafe home access surface
items.claim: The fetched home text on 24 Sep did not show the Join Waitlist string observed on 20 Sep; this does not establish that the waitlist ended or that signup is open.

items.title: Bounded Jev freshness and change-detection pass
items.claim: The bounded 24 Sep report documents two correction triggers and preserves earlier alternatives and product audit dates, without a new account test, benchmark, or full audit.

items.title: TypeSafe API reference
items.claim: Documents the direct POST request, typed questions, model response, token usage, and 401/422/429/529 errors used to design the protocol.

items.title: TypeSafe primitives
items.claim: Defines Choice, Score, and Noul boundaries, including an explicit Choice alternative when the set may be incomplete.

items.title: TypeSafe confidence
items.claim: Choice confidence summarizes the returned distribution and is not a correctness guarantee.

items.title: TypeSafe models
items.claim: Displays jev-1.13.0, direct input-token list pricing, context limits, and dynamic rate-limit caveat; account charges and eligibility are not established.

items.title: Jev 1.13 jaggedness
items.claim: Vendor-described literal, numeric, state, and adversarial failure modes inform challenge-case design, not measured rates.

items.title: TypeSafe legal index
items.claim: Links current MCA, privacy policy, and DPA; route-specific retention and account terms remain checks before real data.

items.title: Support-ticket workload-evaluation protocol
items.claim: The published method has blank result cells and makes no claim of an authenticated Jev call, workload performance, or production suitability.

items.title: kev
items.claim: Independent Jev-like model/runtime; Kev-4B card provides Apache-2.0 weights, not TypeSafe Jev weights

items.title: clm
items.claim: Independent Jev-like model/head with released weights and System One-shaped route; author-run parity claims not adopted

items.title: laya
items.claim: Independent decision-head project; exact weight licence unresolved

items.title: jeff
items.claim: Independent Qwen adapter with typed readouts; author-run comparison not generalized

items.title: open-decision
items.claim: Local framework/backend substitute, not a Jev-equivalent checkpoint

items.title: browser-use
items.claim: Direct TypeSafe Jev request in browser-action code, not production operation evidence

items.title: json-render
items.claim: Experimental Jev composition via Vercel AI Gateway; no customer deployment proved

items.title: canny
items.claim: Direct Jev advisory integration beside deterministic completion ledger

items.title: agentrun
items.claim: Newly announced adapter with optional live-key path; default demos scripted

items.title: netlify-route
items.claim: Netlify gateway route billed in credits; effective Jev rate unknown

items.title: vercel-route
items.claim: Model listing price conflicts with free-through-25-Sep launch promotion; current charge unknown

items.title: jev-mobile
items.claim: 24 Sep author-reported mobile GUI experiment, not deployed product

items.title: jev-wild
items.claim: 24 Sep paper reports a 2,170-project dataset, not independently verified products

items.title: Jevmail
items.claim: README documents read-only Gmail triage using Vercel Jev; no-key preview is simulated.

items.title: DocJev
items.claim: Local extraction followed by Jev document category/split judgments; optional cloud OCR.

items.title: pg-jev
items.claim: SQL Jev judgments with privileged Postgres requirements and off-host row implications.

items.title: Jev Comment Triage
items.claim: WordPress plugin documents held comments, asynchronous judgment, retries and human fallback.

items.title: LocalJev
items.claim: Local TypeSafe-shaped bridge; generated JSON probabilities are not direct logit readout.

items.title: Open-Jev
items.claim: Independent Qwen adapters, separate base weights and local API.

items.title: NanoJev
items.claim: Independent game-control artifact and local readout; benchmarks task-specific.

items.title: Vercel Jev model
items.claim: 25 Sep display Free for TypeSafe AI and DigitalOcean provider rows; promotion ends 25 Sep, post-price unknown.

items.title: Vercel general pricing
items.claim: General credits/tiers are separate from post-promotion Jev rate.

items.claim: Native search returned 403; current post coverage unknown.
